decisions.context: Cameras operate along production lines that often lack network access. Inference must remain available at the line.
decisions.rationale: Choose local inference to keep inspection available offline. “Composing Deep-Learning Microservices for the Hybrid Internet of Things” and “Three Levels of ML Software” document edge inference; this combination had no attesting sources in the checked design point.
consequences: Provision and update models across devices.
Device compute and storage bound the runtime.

decisions.decision: How should weekly training candidates be evaluated?
decisions.context: Newly labeled images feed a weekly retraining cycle. A candidate needs validation before it replaces the deployed model.

alternatives.label: Metric-driven candidate model evaluation
cons: Does not alone ensure safe rollout

decisions.rationale: Evaluate each weekly candidate offline against held-out examples before selection. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” support evaluation and regression thresholds; both checked combinations warned that workflow coordination must be decided first.

decisions.context: The brief says images are newly labeled each week but does not specify who selects or labels them. The choice affects the quality and effort of each retraining cycle.
decisions.rationale: Use human review as the grounded default because the brief establishes labeling but gives no mechanism for sample selection. “Architecture of a real-world Machine Learning system” and “MLOps Principles” describe human-in-the-loop labeling; active learning remains a possible extension.
consequences: Allocate time for review and label quality checks.
The design space does not determine the labeling workflow details.

decisions.context: The brief fixes retraining at a weekly cadence. A scheduled trigger maps directly to that requirement; monitoring can still inform later changes to the cadence.

alternatives.label: Schedule-based retraining trigger
cons: Does not react immediately to drift

decisions.rationale: Choose the required weekly schedule. “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” and “MLOps Principles” discuss recurring retraining; the checked design point also included this trigger, though it had no source attestation as a complete combination.
consequences: Run training and evaluation on a weekly schedule.
Monitor drift and quality to inform future cadence decisions.

decisions.decision: How should model and training artifacts be tracked?
decisions.context: Weekly retraining produces successive models that must be associated with their training inputs and deployment state. The small team benefits from traceability when investigating regressions.
decisions.rationale: Choose lifecycle traceability to connect each weekly model to its data, training run, and deployment status. “MLOps Principles” and “Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably” support this approach; the checked point was novel and unattested, so keep the implementation proportionate to the small team.
consequences: Record dataset, training, model, and deployment identifiers.
Integrated tracking adds operational setup and maintenance.

decisions.decision: How should model updates reach production devices?
decisions.context: Models are pushed to devices, so releases must account for distributed deployment and recovery if a candidate causes problems. The brief does not describe device connectivity or rollout controls.

alternatives.label: Progressive release automation with rollback
cons: May be difficult across offline devices

decisions.rationale: Choose staged rollout with rollback as the safer release pattern for a distributed device fleet. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Model management, deployment, and monitoring with Azure Machine Learning” support progressive releases; device-specific delivery remains outside the design space evidence.
consequences: Keep a prior model available for recovery.
Define how devices receive updates when connectivity returns.

decisions.context: Devices may be disconnected, while inspection quality and input conditions can change. Monitoring should include changes in inputs and service health; the brief does not state that labels are available at inference time.

alternatives.label: Input and feature-drift monitoring
cons: Drift does not prove quality loss

decisions.rationale: Choose input and feature monitoring as the feasible initial signal when network access and fresh ground truth are uncertain. “Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture” and “MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning” support drift monitoring; monitoring choices can be combined because this dimension has zero exclusivity.
consequences: Collect device observations for later central review.
Add quality monitoring when labels become available.

uncovered: How offline devices receive, authenticate, and resume model updates.
Model family, image preprocessing, and device-specific resource limits.
Label review ownership, image retention, and data access policy.
Workflow execution coordination required by evaluation; the design space point warned this prerequisite was undecided.
Monitoring telemetry transport, alerting, and behavior during network outages.
